title: Moon base: fourteen days of night (one unbroken take)
note: Nov 23, late. One camera take, no cut and no transition effect. The picture is NASA's 4K concept animation 'Living and Working on the Moon' (May 2026), source frames 165-329 run there and back; night_fall.py (specs/night_v11_one.json) works on a 3510x1920 strip of it and moves a 1080x1920 frame across that strip at 1:1. Ours, laid over NASA's picture: the travelling shadow, the night, every lamp and beacon, the stars (real ones from the HYG catalogue, placed for the Sun at ecliptic longitude 292 degrees, mid-January: an assumed date), two landers' engine lights with their exhaust, dust at touchdown, spacecraft crossing in orbit, helmet lamps of people walking and a rover far off. Credit NASA; star positions HYG database (CC BY-SA 4.0). Sound effects are synthesised (sfx.py).

shots.job: This shot follows one night at the base in a single take: the Sun low over the ridge as a lander comes in and the ridge's shadow crosses the base; lamps, helmet lamps and stars in the dark under a crescent Earth; first light on the high ridge and across the plain; the shadow coming back as the camera returns to the Sun and a second lander arrives. So the viewer lives through the night the sentences describe. (NASA concept animation; everything listed in the note added)

lines.say: On most of the Moon, night lasts about fourteen days.
Small landers have survived it by mostly shutting down.
No base with people has yet run through a lunar night.
